title: Cassoulet
subtitle: French Languedoc slow-braised bean stew with duck and sausage
excerpt: The greatest of all bean dishes: white beans slowly braised with duck confit, Toulouse sausage, pork belly, and tomato in a clay pot, topped with a golden breadcrumb crust that is broken and stirred back in through several rounds of baking.

recipe.sourceNotes: Cassoulet is the iconic slow-cooked bean and meat stew of the Languedoc region in southern France, taking its name from the cassole, the earthenware dish in which it is cooked. The dish is the subject of heated regional dispute between Castelnaudary, Carcassonne, and Toulouse, each claiming the authentic version. All versions contain white beans (usually haricot or lingot) and a selection of meats including pork, sausage, and duck confit. The Toulouse version adds lamb; the Carcassonne version adds whole partridge. The defining characteristic is the thick breadcrumb crust that forms on the surface during cooking; it is broken and stirred back in at intervals to enrich the stew, which builds up again with each pass. Cassoulet is a dish of several days in its classic form; a simplified version is achievable in one day.

content.text: Soak the beans overnight; they must be tender before the final baking as they will not soften significantly in the oven. The crust forms during baking and is broken back in at least twice; this is not optional, it is the defining technique. Use good-quality Toulouse sausage rather than ordinary pork sausage; the herbed, coarsely ground meat is essential to the finished flavour.

items.preparation: dried; soaked overnight in cold water; drained
Toulouse sausage or coarse-ground pork sausage
confit preferred; fresh works but add 30 minutes extra cooking
for the crust; broken back in 2 to 3 times during baking

content.text: Drain the soaked beans and simmer in fresh unsalted water for 45 to 60 minutes until just tender but not falling apart. Drain. Brown the sausages and pork belly in a large ovenproof pot. Remove. Cook the onion and garlic in the pork fat for 8 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tomato puree, stock, thyme, bay, and drained beans. Return the meats and nestle in the duck legs. Bring to a simmer. Season. Preheat the oven to 160°C / fan 140°C / gas 3.

Scatter the breadcrumbs over the top. Bake uncovered for 45 minutes until a crust forms. Break the crust and stir it in. Bake for 30 more minutes. Break the crust and stir again. Bake a final 30 minutes until a deep golden crust forms. Rest 15 minutes and serve.
